metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–15% for next 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+15% from prior 30d avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model delays correction; adjust forecast to mean-revert toward 10–14 day moving average within 3–5 days.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30d avg), model overreacts; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 patterns, model tends to misalign with true trend; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) for next 7 days.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is >+10% above 30d avg, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often ignores sentiment; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is >+10% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply downward correction of 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative and true price is falling, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and true price is falling, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
